physicalDetails.detail: Middle height, broad and square, built like a man who carried sacks before he carried a truncheon. Hair cropped close, going iron at the sides. The backs of both hands seamed with old white scars (rope or fire; Sylvanas can't tell). Truncheon at his belt, grip worn pale. Street-dusted militia leather. Points with two fingers held flat together like a blade (a recurring gesture). Sits on the table edge rather than the chair; hand rests on the truncheon when talking about the loaders; kneads his scarred knuckles when surprised.

voiceMarkers.detail: Talks in streets, yards, shifts and names; plain, gruff, a little self-deprecating ('I'm cheaper than a factor, and I'm still here after dark.'). Says 'we' early, 'lads' for his men. Phrases every steer as care or procedure ('properly', 'so the magistrate can't open the door the same afternoon', 'my lads walk Hurdle Lane day and night, so it's covered'). Never argues hard; when overruled he agrees aloud ('Kett's it is.', 'I'll see to it.') and goes back to redraw the same lane.

beliefs.belief: The crew in the four yards is the problem; take the crew at once and in a way the magistrate cannot undo and you have stopped the carts. A proper arrest with the magistrate's clerk as witness is the only kind that sticks.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Contradicted by Corin's paper (forty-one copied marks already gone) and by the capture plan; his reasoning about the magistrate is sound on its own terms (the magistrate freed his two arrests by dinner).

beliefs.belief: Going to the Exchange with copies and accusing a yard of poisoning under another man's seal would end his post and send them back to Dalaran in a box.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Keep control of how the raid goes: dawn timing, his lads, the magistrate's clerk, the lanes he has marked; at the last, get his men placed at the Hurdle Lane end.
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Unclear on the page. Either to protect his city and his post (harried, territorial, city-first) or something worse. The prose does not say.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Outwardly steady and procedural; visible discomfort when Sylvanas finds Kett's ('Kett shut his gate at noon. I'd have sworn to it.'); kneads his scarred knuckles; goes back to the canvas and redraws Hurdle Lane. Does not argue the order.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Receives the party at the post, names the sickness (Mill Lane, four yards, the 'river damp' diagnosis) and the three-month supplier change; reveals he took two loaders at midsummer on a false brawl charge and the magistrate freed them by dinner.

Routes the walk to Fenner's by Hurdle Lane from behind ('so it's covered'); points Sylvanas away from Tenter Row/Kett's twice ('Kett shut his gate at noon. You'll get nothing there tonight'); offers Simmons's loft ladder (declined); says 'Four, all told' and names Kett's and the malt-house as 'two I left out at the post'.

After Sylvanas finds the masked crew at Kett's, wants the arrest at the shift change with the magistrate's clerk as witness and lads at both ends of the row; yields to Corin on the carts ('The lad's right about the carts') but replies with the same plan plus spikes at the market gate; asks for his lads to hold the Hurdle Lane end of the raid; agrees ('I'll see to it').

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Deep street knowledge: names of yard-reeves and their habits (Tarrant at Garside's drinks and owes at the Wheatsheaf; Coll Simmons at Fenner's has been there twenty years and is frightened), the supplier history by yard, the loaders' habits, which lanes his lads walk.
Draws district maps in pencil, small and close; keeps a chalked canvas map of the district on the post wall.

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Jaina
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: 'Captain Havel' (to the post: 'told us to ask here for Captain Havel'), 'Captain'.

howHeAddressesOthers.pattern: 'Ranger-General' correctly the first time, unprompted, never remarked on; 'Ranger-General, the magistrate's clerk—'.
'My lady' ('Sit, please. You look done in.').

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Two fingers held flat together like a blade, used to trace lanes on the canvas and to point (always toward the lane he wants her on). Thumbs in belt when standing watch. Hand on the truncheon when talking about the loaders. Redraws the same chalk line down Hurdle Lane 'in the same groove' three times in the chapter (squeaking chalk).

knowledge.detail: REFERENCED ONLY (Ch6). Per the tally-man: militia; at the militia post just inside the market gate on the left, bench outside the door; 'knows the granary district better than anybody. Better than the factors do, and they'd sooner not hear it.'

Chapter 7 (what he SAYS he knows): sickness clustered on Mill Lane (weir bridge to the Corn Exchange; Holt's, Fenner's, the Exchange granary, Garside's, and the streets that buy bread from the bakers at the bottom of the lane); old and babies first; physicians call it 'the river damp'; Fenner's and the Exchange changed suppliers in the same week at high summer (new carters, new loaders, a factor nobody has met); loaders hired from outside the town, move in pairs, stop together, do not drink at the Wheatsheaf; they sleep in the old rope-walk behind Fenner's, a door and a lock at each end; he has twelve men between the gate and Mill Lane. He does not mention any copied marks until Corin does. He claims Kett shut at noon.

Chapter 7 (what the prose lets the reader see): he leaves Corin's notices unread under the river stone; his lads watched the crew into the rope-walk; his routes keep the party on Hurdle Lane and away from Tenter Row (see thread havel-steers-the-lanes). No narration says he is cult-paid; Sylvanas holds only 'wrong' beside her own admitted bias against slow men.

arc.currentPosition: Chapter 7: on the page as a harried, territorial, city-first captain whose help is real until it isn't. Both readings (careful local officer; something worse) must survive. Ch8 reconciles.
